transcript.text: We do online personal training for
people who ride horses. If we have an
opportunity for a trainer who's going to
come work with us and that opportunity
is capped at like 60 grand a year, how
do you retain good people on an
opportunity that's smaller?
>> They're remote, right?
>> Yeah.
>> Well, it's work in your pajamas and work
on fitness, which is like a lot of
people's dream. So, this is a mistake
that I made early on, so hopefully you
won't make it. Is that you need to
advertise for that type of person. That
type of person does not care about
business. They're not somebody who cares
about career path. They care about
impact and doing things they love and
having flexibility in their life. You
have to think about like, what is the
type of person I want to attract? Like
if you're trying to attract you, you
wouldn't take this opportunity, so stop
trying to sell you.
Does that make sense?
>> Yeah, it does.
>> Yeah, so you just need to change the
messaging from the recruiting
perspective.
